title: Joints & ligaments anatomy
description: Where bones meet: cartilage cushions, capsules contain, ligaments guide — the knee is the classic teaching joint because every principle is visible in it.

questions.question: What holds a joint together?
questions.answer: A joint may be supported by a capsule, ligaments, tendons and nearby muscles. Exact stabilizers vary between joints; the knee also has menisci and cruciate ligaments.

questions.question: What do the ACL and PCL do in the knee?
questions.answer: The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments resist different directions of tibial translation and help stabilize the knee during movement.

questions.question: What is the anterior cruciate ligament?
questions.answer: From lateral femoral condyle to anterior tibial plateau. Function: Blocks anterior tibial translation; pivots in rotation.

questions.question: Where is the posterior cruciate ligament located?
questions.answer: Medial femoral condyle to posterior tibia. Function: Blocks posterior tibial slide (dashboard injury).

questions.question: What is the function of the menisci (medial & lateral)?
questions.answer: Function: Load sharing, shock absorption, joint lubrication. Fibrocartilage crescents on the tibial plateau.
